explanation: erdosproblems.com/49: 'The primes are such an example. Are they the largest possible?' The Lean statement asks whether f(N) = π(N) for all N ≥ 2, where f(N) is the maximum size of A ⊆ [1,N] with φ strictly increasing on A. This is the natural reading (N = 1 excluded since {1} beats π(1) = 0). As a sanity check I computed f(N) by longest strictly increasing subsequence of φ(1..N) and found f(N) = π(N) for all 2 ≤ N ≤ 3000, so the question is not trivially refuted (in contrast with the non-decreasing version, where OEIS A365339 shows π(N) + 64 for large N). Faithful.
